summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, and glaucoma was admitted for acute onset blurry vision in her left eye, which was her better-seeing eye with only 20% visual acuity and severe peripheral vision loss at baseline. Imaging revealed a small chronic brain infarct but no acute stroke, and ophthalmology suspected worsening proliferative diabetic retinopathy as the cause of vision change. She also presented with uncontrolled diabetes, acute kidney injury, and hypovolemia, likely exacerbated by diuretic use. Her diuretics were held, IV fluids were given cautiously, and her kidney function improved. Blood and urine cultures showed no infection. She was stabilized, educated on symptom monitoring, and discharged with plans for ophthalmology follow-up and medication adjustments.
